messages:
maya: Heads-up — when we onboarded the distilled-7B-int8 model into the eval harness I noticed the pass@k curve vs model confidence looks inverted for low-confidence buckets. feels like a calibration/aggregation bug.

cheng: Can you paste the plot or numbers? is this during sampling eval or deterministic greedy?

maya: Sampling. Attached snapshot: low-prob samples (0.0-0.2) have higher pass@1 than 0.2-0.4 which doesn't make sense. sample counts per bucket look ok.

sam: that often comes from how we aggregate per-example top-k counts. if we compute pass@k on the pooled sample set instead of per-example samples it can bias low-prob buckets.

maya: here's the relevant snippet from runner v0.42:```python
# naive pooled pass@k
for k in ks:
    successes = 0
    for sample in all_samples:
        if gold in sample.topk(k):
            successes += 1
    passk = successes / total_samples
```

liam: thats the bug — pooled pass@k needs to be computed per problem then averaged. otherwise items with many samples dominate.

maya: agreed. expected implementation is per-example pass@k then mean:```python
# per-example pass@k
per_example = []
for ex in examples:
    succ = any(gold in s.topk(k) for s in ex.samples)
    per_example.append(int(succ))
passk = sum(per_example) / len(per_example)
```

eval-bot: eval-run 2024-08-15T12:03:12Z: distilled-7B-int8 sampling eval finished; metrics: pooled_pass@1=0.42, per_example_pass@1=0.31, bscore_mean=0.71

cheng: that explains the inversion then. pooled_pass@1 overstated success for low-confidence clusters if some prompts produced lots of degenerate repeats.

sam: two follow-ups: 1) we should add a unit test in metrics_test to assert pooled vs per_example divergence below a threshold; 2) add a CI check to ensure pass@k is computed per-example for all sampling-based evaluations.

maya: also observed BERTScore drift after quantization — could be tokenization differences? but the BScore impl is fine. suspect float precision in similarity matrix when int8 kernels run on-device and then rescored on CPU with different rounding.

liam: add a recalculation sanity check: compute embeddings in 32-bit for scoring step even if generation used int8 kernels. that should avoid numeric drift.

cheng: for calibration curve: proposal -> compute confidence per example as max token log-prob of the predicted sequence (or mean token prob), bucket by quantiles, then report per-bucket pass@k and reliability (accuracy vs confidence). Also try temperature scaling post-hoc to see if it fixes miscalibration.

maya: agreed. I'll open a PR with: fix per-example pass@k, force scoring in fp32, add calibration curve code + small notebook, add CI test asserting monotonicity of pass@k vs k and non-decreasing accuracy with confidence buckets.

sam: do we want to also change dashboard? current per-route panels show pooled pass@k only. we should add per-example_pass@k and a calibration panel (confidence vs accuracy) + probe for quantized variants.

liam: yep — mark as product-req for eng-dashboard. low priority but good to have before more model bring-ups.

maya: I'll tag PR and link notebooks here when ready. thanks team. :thumbsup:
